_provenance: For --scene pick_place --target-object <id> (sim/scripts/run_robot129_ros_webrtc.py) and tools/generate_s2_cube_candidates.py's generalized candidate generator (docs/dev_guide_paper_core_and_dashboard_plan.md §8 'grasp' scenario). All these shapes are AUTHORED simulation objects, not measurements of a real physical prop -- same status as the existing cube/hammer numbers in scene_geometry.json, not a AGENTS.md 'never guess hardware' case. mass_kg for every entry is size scaled from the original cube's own mass_kg=0.08 at size_m=0.035 in scene_geometry.json, at a constant assumed density of ~1866 kg/m^3 (0.08 / 0.035^3) -- i.e. not independently guessed per object, just carried through consistently so heavier/lighter feels physically plausible relative to the one real reference point. All sizes fit within the gripper's ~0.07m max opening (2 x joint7's 0.035m range) with margin, per the plan's own constraint.

cube_35.note: unchanged original pick_place target -- --target-object cube_35 (the default) must spawn byte-for-byte the same object as before this option existed.

flat_box.note: flat/asymmetric -- see research/src/mpg/curobo_bridge/frames.py 'KNOWN MISMATCH' docstring before claiming a grasp of this one is a narrow-side grasp; verify against the real closing axis (local Y), not the scored one (local X).

ball.note: stretch target per the plan -- a sphere has no stable top-down parallel-jaw grasp orientation the way a box/cylinder does; existing grasp_candidates.py's top-down generator was written for box/cylinder profiles and has not been validated against a sphere. Expect this one to need extra work, not a guaranteed drop-in.
